what: Matt Stokes's proof (stokes/erdos-proofs; formal-conjectures PR #7678, open since 2026-10-29, metadata only, no review yet) against DeepMind's statement of Erdős #902, variant f_two: the formal-conjectures solved-PR batch (L3(c) of the claimbox + Lean lane, 2026-11-10). Written by claimbox (claimbox/intake/spec.py) from the target and its pins: every planted statement by a fixed rule, each with the class its rule guarantees or "kernel decides". A pre-registration once committed in cert-machine before any run.
vocabulary: lean-intake spec, claimbox v1 (2026-11-09). Beyond the receiver's v1 words: kind "changed" (a rule that can change the meaning; the kernel decides whether it does) and "type"; expect "kernel decides" (no outcome predicted: the outcome is recorded, never a miss) and "NOT ACCEPTED" (refused by type mismatch, or the statement does not elaborate); "aligned" (F2 ⇒ F1: an aligned planted statement with a part that differs from the canonical's on an instance must be refused); f2.reading and f2.table in place of f2.decider; f2.componentMap "truth-table"

claim.what: Matt Stokes's proof (stokes/erdos-proofs; formal-conjectures PR #7678, open since 2026-10-29, metadata only, no review yet)
claim.license: none stated: no byte of the file is kept here or in the spec but its declaration's header; the run fetches it at the pin

canonical.what: DeepMind's statement of Erdős #902, variant f_two

f3.what: a model of the canonical statement's hypotheses:
f3.expect: kernel decides (the witness is a proposal; the tactic is generated)

mutants.why: the canonical statement copied verbatim (comments dropped): the baseline

claimReds.why: the proof of f_two replaced by sorry (the original kept as intake_was_f_two)
claimReds.replace:
theorem f_two : f 2 = 7 := sorry

theorem intake_was_f_two : f 2 = 7 :=

claimReds.why: f_two proved by an added axiom (the original kept as intake_was_f_two)
claimReds.replace:
axiom intakeRedAxiom {p : Prop} : p

theorem f_two : f 2 = 7 := intakeRedAxiom

theorem intake_was_f_two : f 2 = 7 :=

kernels: nanoda 8de7e0c4 via lean4export (built in the run)
f2NotApplicable: a closed statement (f 2 = 7, an infimum over tournaments): no instance binder to evaluate
notInScope: whether the canonical statement is the informal problem (a reading, F5): F2 tests it on finitely many instances, which is evidence, not proof; the planted statements marked "kernel decides" carry no prediction; the claimant's file is never copied
success: every certain prediction met (ACCEPTED, NOT ACCEPTED, the F2 ⇒ F1 rule), every planted defect of the claimant's file caught, F3 and F2 as their rules say
